files.purpose: Defines the thread's changes view and the AppKit popover that hosts it. DiffInspector is the 640 by 540 content: a header with a turn picker ('All changes' or 'Turn N' over runtime.turnsWithChanges()), a file count and +/- stat, an ellipsis menu with Expand all / Collapse all and an X that clears runtime.isDiffVisible; below it either 'Reading the diff…', the 'No changes yet' empty state, or a lazy list of collapsible DiffFileCard rows, loaded via runtime.parsedDiff after a 180 ms delay unless the diff is cached, merged with the patches of a tapped tool row (focusedFiles) and scrolled to the first focused file. DiffLinesView renders hunks as header/tinted/plain sections, capped at 200 lines behind a 'Show all N lines' button, and DiffPopoverCoordinator drives a semitransient NSPopover from runtime.isDiffVisible / diffOpenRequest with pass-through mouse and Escape monitors and session counters that stop a stale close from clobbering a fresh open.

files.purpose: The Settings MCP page. It stacks a lead card ('Connected servers lead' with a hover info popover of three facts), a Connected section listing connected catalog servers sorted by name (switch, tool count and version, a menu with Refresh / Show tools / Disconnect), the Custom section of the user's own servers with an Add server row, and one two-column LazyVGrid per MCP category of server cards whose button reads Connect, Sign in, Waiting/Connecting, Fix it, Try again or Sign in again by MCPConnectionState; a newly connected card celebrates for 900 ms with a SettleChime before moving to Connected unless Reduce Motion is on. It also hosts MCPCustomEditor (name, stdio/http kind, command, one-argument-per-line args, URL, environment variables or headers whose values can be locked into the Keychain, save through mcp.saveCustom and saveCustomValues, refresh when an edited server was connected), the hover-or-click info popover with Connects/Needs/Tools/docs link, FlowLayout chips, and MCPIcon.

SOURCE FACT: B3 DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift changes ChromeCard to take `var lazy = false` and build a LazyVStack only when lazy is true, a VStack otherwise, with the comment 'Use lazy only for cards that list a long, uniform, growing collection. files.purpose: The thread sidebar, shown in the window column or in the Threads popover (inPopover, which closes on selection). It holds the 'Search threads' field with arrow-key result walking, the bell ActivityViewToggle, a lazy list in either the project layout (projects with counts, pinned then open threads, a Settled header that folds settled threads) or the activity layout ('Needs attention', 'Pinned', Today/Yesterday/weekday/date groups, Settled), helper rows with a dotted connector, Hydra head glyph cards (twelve shown, the rest behind a chevron) and folded-helper stubs, then 'Add project' (NSOpenPanel) and 'Settings' with an update dot. One list-wide 4 pt DragGesture reorders open thread rows live among their peers with spring slides and a haptic per swap; rows show hover actions, a settle check, an archive button with a Genie ghost, a fold chevron, rename/delete/archive popovers anchored on the row, and context menus built from snapshots through SidebarMenuRequests. Placement, helper grouping, item and search caches keep re-renders cheap, and MinuteClock ticks relative times once a minute.

feature_notes: B2->B3 churn is 3 lines: +1 at B3 :124 `.pointerStyle(drag.id != nil ? .grabActive : nil)` on the list's LazyVStack (after `.coordinateSpace(name: Self.listSpace)`), -1 B2 :775 `NSCursor.closedHand.push()` in dragChanged's first-grab branch, -1 B2 :805 `NSCursor.pop()` in dragEnded. SOURCE FACT: the grabbing cursor is no longer an AppKit cursor-stack push at the grab and pop at release; it is a SwiftUI pointer style that the list declares while `drag.id` is non-nil and withdraws (nil) otherwise. The user still sees a grabbing hand while dragging a row, but the push/pop pairing (and the 'never pop without a push' guard it needed) is gone, and the style belongs to the list view's region rather than the process-wide cursor.

Line map B2->B3: :1-123 unchanged; :124-774 +1; :775 deleted; :776-804 unchanged; :805 deleted; :806-2696 -1 (B3 has 2695 lines). PR-SIDEBAR-049 (which specifies the push/pop) and UI-SIDEBAR-060 (whose notes say the cursor becomes the closed hand for the drag's whole life, citing :803-812) change behaviour; UI-SIDEBAR-005 (the list, :101-147) gains the pointer-style state; every other record citing a line at or after :124 needs its numbers re-cited only. Records citing SidebarView lines only in non-evidence fields (UI-MCP-046 notes, PR-SETTINGS-034, PR-SETTINGS-117, UI-STORE-002 notes, UI-THEME-050 notes) shift too.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: whether SwiftUI keeps the .grabActive pointer style while the pointer leaves the list's LazyVStack during an active drag (B2's NSCursor push held until release wherever the pointer went). The source does not say; only a macOS 15+ runtime check of Droppy Code 1.7.0 would settle it, and the port's Windows scoping of the grabbing cursor depends on it.
